title: Maximum Alternating Subarray Sum
statement:
For a non-empty contiguous block of `nums` running from index `i` to index `j`, its alternating sum adds its first element, subtracts the second, adds the third, and so on with the signs switching: `nums[i] - nums[i + 1] + nums[i + 2] - ... ± nums[j]`. The sign of each element depends on its position inside the block, not on its index in `nums`.

Return the largest alternating sum over all such blocks of `nums`.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every block and summing it with switching signs costs O(n²) or worse. Instead, look at the blocks that end at index `i`: in each of them `nums[i]` is either added or subtracted. A block where `nums[i]` is added either starts at `i` or extends a block whose last element was subtracted; a block where `nums[i]` is subtracted must extend a block whose last element was added (a block cannot start with a minus). Two running values, one per sign, are enough.

## Approach

1. Start at index 0: the only block ending there is `[nums[0]]`, so `plus = nums[0]`, `minus = -Infinity` (impossible), `best = nums[0]`.
2. For each later `num = nums[i]`, the best block ending here with `num` added is `max(minus, 0) + num`: extend a minus-ending block, or start fresh.
3. The best block ending here with `num` subtracted is `plus - num`.
4. Replace `plus` and `minus` with the new values (computed from the old ones) and update `best`.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, -1, 1, 2]`. Start with `plus = 3`, `minus = -Infinity`, `best = 3`. At `-1`: `plus = max(-Infinity, 0) - 1 = -1`, `minus = 3 - (-1) = 4`, `best = 4`. At `1`: `plus = 4 + 1 = 5`, `minus = -1 - 1 = -2`, `best = 5`. At `2`: `plus = max(-2, 0) + 2 = 2`, `minus = 5 - 2 = 3`, so `best` stays `5` (the block `[3, -1, 1]`).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant work per element.
- Space: O(1): only three running values.

## Pitfalls

- A block cannot begin with a subtracted element, so `minus` must not start from 0; use `-Infinity` for "no such block".
- Compute both new values from the old `plus` and `minus` before overwriting either.
- The answer may be negative (all values negative and a single element is best); do not start `best` at 0.
- Sums reach about 10^10, beyond 32-bit integers, which is why the signature returns `long`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `plus` | best alternating sum of a block ending at the current index with that element added |
| `minus` | best alternating sum of a block ending at the current index with that element subtracted |
| `best` | largest alternating sum seen so far |
| `num` | the current element `nums[i]` |
| `nextPlus`, `nextMinus` | the new `plus` and `minus` computed from the old ones |

narration.2: The only block ending at index 0 is nums[0] alone, with a plus sign.
narration.3: No block can end at index 0 with a minus sign, so mark it impossible.
narration.4: The single first element is the best block seen so far.
narration.6: Extend the picture one index at a time.
narration.8: Adding num: extend a block whose last element was subtracted, or start a new block at num if that is better.
narration.9: Subtracting num: it must extend a block whose last element was added.
narration.10: Commit the new plus value, computed from the old values.
narration.12: A block ending here with either sign may be the best so far.
narration.14: Return the largest alternating sum found.
